brief: Goldman's 2027 outlook (Growing Pains) argues the AI investment impulse, which drove 21% of this year's US GDP growth, 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth and 92% of the S&P's market cap gain (41% year to date), is set to peak in early 2027, defined as AI investment's growth rate as a share of GDP. That peak is a manageable event for the economy but a bigger test for markets, because AI's contribution to earnings and market value has run far ahead of its contribution to GDP. Global AI capex still rises from about $1 trillion to $1.8 trillion by 2027, but its contribution to US GDP growth peaks near 2pp in Q1 2027 then fades to zero by late 2028, and S&P earnings growth is forecast to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. The main risk channel is financial conditions: AI financing needs keep building, AI investment-grade credit spreads have widened to Liberation Day rout levels (140bp versus 100bp elsewhere), and Goldman expects further widening. Its most constructive call is duration, with the 10-year yield seen at 4.6% by end-2027. It also expects a weaker dollar, stays bearish the euro until France's election, and recommends equity-put and rates hedges against a bigger aggregate shock.
